concern.concern: Proof 2.1 applies the planar disk-slide supplier and says, “Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately.” The cited lem-marked-planar-cut-surface-regions-are-realized-by-disk-slides explicitly requires its inner faces to come from distinct disks. The proof should explain the successive one-face planar regions that permit repeated disk labels, rather than apply that supplier directly to the whole cap.

original_concerns.reason: The named planar supplier requires all inner faces to have distinct disk labels, whereas the cap may contain both faces of one retained disk. Merely saying processed separately does not exhibit legal successive applications. The missing induction uses the supplier only with r=1, where the moving disk and each retained disk have distinct labels. It leaves the general closed-manifold and full-module claims intact.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: [F6]'s planar construction slides $D_i$ across those faces until its outer rim is precisely $\partial D_i'$, followed by the empty-annulus isotopy. Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: Apply [F6]'s planar supplier successively with exactly two inner faces, rather than once to this whole cap. Choose a finite tree of disjoint joining bands in the cap, rooted at its unique $D_i$ face, and process it outward from the root. At each stage the frontier of a small neighborhood of the processed subtree is the moving rim. A thin neighborhood of that moving face, the next unused face and their joining band is a disk with two holes whose interior misses every other current face and z. Its two labels are the current moving disk and a retained $D_j$ with $j\ne i$, so the supplier's distinct-disk hypothesis holds with $r=1$. Its completed slide preserves the cut ball and the retained disks. Use its finger-retraction identification, supported at that face and band, to carry the unprocessed cap and its remaining faces to the new cut-ball boundary; outside that neighborhood the unused faces are unchanged. Thus the next stage has the same description. If both faces of a retained disk occur, the second remains an unused face of that retained disk and is processed by a later two-face application; it is never paired with its other face in one application. A tiny auxiliary trivial arc near z, with second endpoint w, can be fixed before this construction and missed by all these cap neighborhoods, so the supplier's marked arc condition is retained. After finitely many stages the moving rim is the frontier of the whole tree neighborhood, and the remaining empty annulus in the cap gives the isotopy to $\partial D_i'$.
